title: Design and Synthesis of a Reconfigurable DNA Accordion Rack
protocol: Download and install caDNAno 2.0 software.
Open caDNAno and click the Square Tool to add a new part with a square lattice.
Number each beam of the accordion rack and draw on the left lattice panel.
Click the pencil tool and draw each beam on the right edit panel.
Break beams every 32 bp for joints between adjacent beams.
Place staple crossovers in the same position as the joints.
Use the Insert Tool and the Pencil Tool to let the joints have additional single-stranded crossovers.
Connect the joints with the Pencil Tool; each beam has seven joints.
Generate scaffold crossovers to merge the scaffolds into a single loop using the reported scaffold routing algorithm.
Ensure that the minimum binding domain between scaffold and staple strands is at least 8 bp.
Place unused scaffolds at vertices located on opposite sides of the accordion rack.
Click the Break Tool to break strands where staple strands are circular or longer than 60 bp.
Design DNA lock strands by breaking 8 bp of a staple DNA region to make a sticky part and deleting 8 bp of a staple DNA region.
Place sequences that are reverse complementary to the sticky parts at both ends of lock strands and connect them by a bridging region, which consists of poly T strands of the desired length.
Add 8 bp of toehold sequences at the end of DNA locks for strand displacement.
Prepare poly A strands which are reverse complementary to the bridging region.
Design strands that are reverse complementary to the DNA locks for the reconfiguration experiment.
Click the Sequence Tool and click scaffold DNA.
Choose the scaffold as standard M13mp18.
Click the Export Tool and save sequence in csv format.
Download and install the oxDNA package.
Make starting configuration files from the caDNAno file using python script 'cadnano_interface.py'.
Generate topology file and configuration file.
Rotate and move each beam to the desired lattice structure in the configuration file.
Relax the structure using the script provided in the oxDNA package.
Run molecular dynamics simulation for ten million steps using the relaxed configuration file.
Save data every 5000 or 10000 steps.
Download and install the latest version of cogli.
Run the cogli with the topology and configuration files from the oxDNA simulation.
Hide the box by pressing b.
Purchase DNA staples from an oligonucleotide provider.
Adjust the concentration of DNA staples to 100 μM using nuclease-free water.
Pool each DNA strand that constitutes a ‘free state’ structure into one tube.
Adjust the concentration of pooled strands to 2 μM for each strand.
Pool DNA lock strands by length and number of lock sites into tubes.
Adjust the concentration of pooled lock strands to 2 μM for each strand.
Add poly A strands complementary to the bridging region at the same concentration.
Pool strands that are reverse complementary to the DNA lock strands by length into tubes and adjust the concentration to 2 μM for each strand.
Prepare MgCl2 solution of 300 nM by mixing 70 μL of nuclease-free water and 30 μL of the 1 μM MgCl2 solution.
Prepare a 5x Tris EDTA solution by mixing 95 μL of nuclease-free water and 5 μL of the 100x Tris EDTA solution.

Add 2 μL of staple DNA, 1.1 μL of MgCl2 solution, 2 μL of Tris EDTA solution, 7.6 μL of nuclease-free water, and 7.3 μL of scaffold DNA of which the concentration is 110 nM to make 20 μL of mixed stock.
Set the final concentration of the scaffold DNA to 40 nM, staple DNA to 200 nM, MgCl2 to 16 mM, and Tris EDTA solution to 0.5x.
Rapidly heat the mixed stock solution in a thermal cycler to 80 °C.
Cool the heated solution from 80 °C to 60 °C at a rate of 4 min per °C.
Cool the solution from 60 °C to 4 °C at a rate of 40 min per °C.
Prepare target-buffer by mixing 5.5 μL of 300 nM MgCl2, 10 μL of 5x Tris EDTA, and 84.5 μL of nuclease-free water.
Mix 20 μL of the synthesized structure with 20 μL of precipitation-buffer.
Spin the mixed stock at 16000 x g at 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant and dissolve the pellet in target-buffer.
Synthesize the structure without DNA locks for the configuration experiment.
Prepare DNA lock strands from Section 3.
Add 2 μL of DNA lock strands into 20 μL of the synthesized structure.
Incubate the sample at 50 °C for 3 minutes, then slowly cool down to 25 °C at a rate of 3.3 °C/minute.
Incubate the sample at 50 °C for 7.5 minutes, then slowly cool down to 25 °C at a rate of 1.32 °C/minute.
Incubate the sample at 50 °C for 15 minutes, then slowly cool down to 25 °C at a rate of 0.66 °C/minute.
Incubate the sample at 50 °C for 30 minutes, then slowly cool down to 25 °C at a rate of 0.33 °C/minute.
Store the sample at 4 °C right after DNA locks strands are added.
Rapidly cool down the sample to 4°C after the attaching step to prevent unwanted denaturation.
Synthesize DNA locks of the desired length for reconfiguration experiments.
Prepare reverse complementary strands from Section 3.
Add 2 μL of reverse complementary strands to 20 μL of synthesized structure.
Incubate the sample for 0 minutes at 4°C after adding reverse complementary strands.
Heat the sample to 40°C and slowly cool down to 20°C for 12, 60, 120, and 240 minutes respectively.
Rapidly cool down the sample to 4°C after detaching step to prevent unwanted denaturation.
Prepare a 1.25 M NaOH solution by mixing 87.5 μL of nuclease-free water with 12.5 μL of 10 M NaOH solution.
Add 1 μL of 1.25 M NaOH solution to 50 μL of the 2% uranyl formate solution.
Vortex the mixed solution for 3 minutes and centrifuge at maximum speed for 3 minutes.
Deposit 3 μL of purified sample on a glow-discharged TEM grid for 3 minutes.
Rapidly wash out excess with filter paper after depositing the sample.
Deposit 7 μL of prepared uranyl formate solution for 30 seconds.
Rapidly wash out with filter paper.
Measure the length and angle of the accordion structure imaged by TEM.
Use Atto 550 and Atto 647N dye, for which the Förster distance is 6.5 nm.
Replace Staple 58 and Staple 117 in Table 1 with fluorescently labelled strands.
Synthesize the structure with fluorescently labelled strands by the method described in Section 3.
Measure the concentration of the purified sample.
Normalize the sample to 10 nM.
Load 50 μL of normalized sample to the 384 microplates well.
Excite the sample with donor and acceptor dyes at 550 nm.
Measure the fluorescence spectrum from 570 nm to 800 nm with a fluorometer.
Measure the fluorescence spectrum of the donor-only sample in the same way.
Excite the dyes of the sample at 650 nm.
Measure the fluorescence spectrum and measure from 670 nm to 800 nm.
Obtain the standard deviations by repeating the experiment with three samples, which are synthesized and purified separately.
Calculate the FRET efficiency using the ratio A method as described by the equation.
